messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Pause 1.3.0
parts:
Hey guys,

Can you put a quick pause on 1.3.0? To use a quick Linus-isum I've
found a brown-paper bag issue. Should be easy to fix, but if we
release with it, multi_normal will be quite slow.

Cheers,
Marcus

*REALLY* important to include the agrad header files, otherwise it
will silently fall back to using the non-vectorized versions of
functions. This just happened to me with the newly minted
mdivide_left_spd.

Cheers,
Marcus

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Pause 1.3.0
parts:
I pushed the patches for the diff'ed manual (as long as there are no more changes to the .tex files). So you can do

./diff_manual.sh v1.2.0 v1.3.0

There might be an error message if your bash is sufficiently different from my bash, and if so let me know. Also, it seems as if the previous versions of the diff'ed manual were only getting uploaded to Google Code without having a link on mc-stan.org, so it is unlikely that anyone would find them unless they knew where to look.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Pause 1.3.0
parts:
On 4/10/13 6:12 PM, Daniel Lee wrote:
> So, are we good?
>
>
> On Wed, Apr 10, 2013 at 4:57 PM, Michael Betancourt <betan...@gmail.com <mailto:betan...@gmail.com>> wrote:
>
> I gotta say, as much as I whined about unit tests the other day,

You weren't been in NY long enough for your
whine to really evolve.

> implementing the file_include tests revealed a ton
> of fragile includes in the refactored HMC code.

Errors tend to be easier to find with unit tests than
any other way. It's the only way to write even reasonably
reliable code. We're still a long way away from a rock
solid set of unit tests, but what we have has saved me
more times than I can count.

- Bob

>
> add_binary("owenst");

If owenst is a function that takes two scalar args
and returns a scalar, then yes, that's all you need.

The alphabetization is just to make it more human
readable.

- Bob
